events.reason: Follow-up of hepatitis B-associated polyarteritis nodosa

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology clinic. Date of service 1/22/2025. Copy to primary care.

Follow-up for polyarteritis nodosa associated with chronic hepatitis B, diagnosed during his October admission with mesenteric involvement.

Interval: completed prednisone taper in mid-November. No abdominal pain since discharge. No fever, rash, testicular pain, new numbness or weakness. Appetite fine. Taking entecavir daily.

Medications: entecavir 0.5 mg daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, risperidone 2 mg daily, diphenhydramine as needed, calcium carbonate as needed. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without livedo or nodules. Neurologic exam without deficit.

Labs: creatinine 1.3.

Assessment: HBV-associated PAN in clinical remission after antiviral therapy and a short steroid course.

Plan: continue entecavir indefinitely. No further immunosuppression. Return in 6 months or sooner for abdominal pain, fever, new rash or neuropathic symptoms.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: No belly pain since the hospital. Saw rheumatology in January (letter received last week): in remission, entecavir indefinitely. Prednisone finished in November; sugars back to his usual. Weight up a little to 72. Takes entecavir every day, says it's the one pill he never misses. Risperidone "most days." No psychiatry.
O: Vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, nontender. Heart regular, lungs clear. Feet intact, pulses good.
A/P:
1. HBV-associated PAN in remission. Entecavir. CMP today for creatinine and liver tests.
2. DM: A1c today. Metformin dose fine for his kidney function.
3. HTN at goal.
4. Schizophrenia: continue risperidone; psychiatry referral information given again.
RTC 3 months, can be video.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from his apartment, sister joined from her phone. Consent for video visit given.
Feels fine. Taking lisinopril, metformin, entecavir daily; risperidone most days. Water intake steady, no headaches or dizziness. CPAP mask cracked; asked for a new prescription for supplies. No abdominal pain, fever, rash.
Appears well on video, speech sparse but organized, not distressed.
A/P: Stable. CPAP supply order faxed to his equipment company. Refills sent for 90 days. Labs and in-person visit in August with eye exam reminder.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: entecavir 0.5 mg and risperidone 2 mg, 90 days each. Seen by video in May, office visit booked for August. Sent per PCP standing order.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Outside optometry office. Dilated exam 7/29/2025. Corrected acuity 20/25 both eyes. Pressures normal. No retinopathy, no macular edema in either eye. Annual follow-up.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare annual wellness visit, first one here.

Health risk review: lives alone in an apartment, sister nearby and involved, helps with groceries and the pill box. Independent with bathing, dressing, cooking simple meals; sister handles bills. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision adequate with glasses. Still drives locally. No alcohol, quit smoking 2017. Walks most days.

Current problems: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, schizophrenia, chronic hepatitis B, polyarteritis nodosa in remission on entecavir, obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, peptic ulcer disease history, right inguinal hernia, resected bronchial carcinoid with prior ectopic ACTH, primary polydipsia.
Meds reconciled: lisinopril 20 daily, metformin 1000 BID, entecavir 0.5 daily, risperidone 2 daily (most days), diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn, calcium carbonate prn.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft, right inguinal hernia reducible. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses palpable, no lesions.
Screens: PHQ-9 4. AUDIT-C 0. Cognition grossly intact on conversation.

Prevention: colonoscopy 2020 normal, next 2030. Shingrix complete. PCV20 2022. Tdap 2019. Flu and COVID this fall. Eye exam done July. Hep C and HIV screens done 2019.

Plan: labs today (A1c, CMP, CBC, lipids, urine microalbumin). Advance directive packet given; he wants his sister as health care agent and will return the form. RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 10/15/2025, arrival 07:50. (Copy received by the practice 2/10/2026.)

Chief complaint: painful, discolored fingers after a night in the cold.

HPI: 52-year-old man with schizophrenia, diabetes and a history of polyarteritis nodosa. Last evening he was driving in the hills when an early-season snowstorm came in; his car got stuck and he spent the night in it. The heater would not stay on and he had no gloves. Found this morning and brought in by ambulance. Severe pain in the fingers.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg BID, risperidone 2 mg daily, diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed, calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed; entecavir per pharmacy record. NKDA. Former smoker, no alcohol.

Vitals: T 35.6 C, BP 135/85, HR 88, RR 16.

Exam: fingers cold, mottled and waxy in appearance, no bleeding, no blisters. Reduced sensation and no capillary refill in the affected fingers. Remainder of the exam unremarkable.

ED course: rapid rewarming of the hands in a circulating water bath at 40 C for 30 minutes with analgesia. After rewarming the affected fingers were still discolored, still numb, and still without capillary refill.

Assessment: severe frostbite of the fingers with tissue necrosis and microvascular thrombosis.

Disposition: admitted to the hospital for further management of frostbite, with hand surgery consultation.

documents.title: Sister calling - hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sister called to let us know Sean got stuck in his car overnight in last week's snow and his fingers were frostbitten. He was in the hospital several days and is home now; a hand surgeon is following him. She does not have discharge papers handy. Scheduled post-hospital visit 11/5. Records release faxed to the hospital.

documents.title: Please reschedule
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Sean, we missed you on November 5. Your doctor would like to check on your hands and your other medicines after your hospital stay. Please call us or reply to set up a time. We also have not received your hospital records yet; if you have any papers from the hospital or the hand surgeon, please bring them.

documents.title: RE: Please reschedule
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry he has had a lot of appointments with the hand doctor. Can we do January? Mornings are best. - his sister

conditions.label: Severe frostbite with tissue necrosis and microvascular thrombosis
conditions.note: left index and middle fingertips; followed by hand surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with sister. Hospital and hand surgery records still not received; history from them.

S: In October he was stuck overnight in his car in the snow without gloves. Went to the ED by ambulance, fingers rewarmed, admitted several days. Says they gave him an IV medicine "to open up the blood flow" for a few days. Most fingers came back. The tips of the left index and middle fingers turned black and dry. Hand surgery sees him every couple of weeks; they plan to trim the dead tips once the line between dead and healthy tissue is complete. Some aching in those fingers, acetaminophen helps. No fever, no drainage. Otherwise taking entecavir, lisinopril, metformin daily, risperidone most days.
O: Vitals as charted. Left index and middle fingertips with dry black eschar, well demarcated, no surrounding redness, swelling or drainage. Light touch reduced at those two tips. Other fingers on both hands warm, pink, normal capillary refill. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft.
A/P:
1. Severe frostbite, left index and middle fingertips, demarcated dry eschar, hand surgery managing. Keep dry and protected, gloves outdoors. Call for redness, swelling, pus or fever. Added to problem list.
2. DM, HTN, PAN on entecavir: A1c, BMP, CBC, hepatic panel today.
3. Schizophrenia: risperidone; discussed safety in winter (charged phone, not driving into the hills in storms).
4. Flu shot offered, declined today.
5. Records request to the hospital and hand surgery sent again.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, yesterday's labs are back. Your diabetes number is in your usual range. Kidney function is stable at your new baseline, sodium is normal, and your blood count and liver tests are normal. Keep taking the entecavir every day. Let us know how the hand surgeon visits go.

documents.title: Refill request - entecavir
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: entecavir 0.5 mg daily, 90 days. Prior authorization renewal also due; submitted and approved. Refill sent.

documents.title: Refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: He needs the metformin and the blood pressure pill again, the pharmacy said they need the doctor. His fingers are still being seen by the hand doctor. - sister

documents.title: RE: Refills
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Refills for metformin and lisinopril sent for 90 days. Thanks for the update; please ask the hand surgeon's office to fax us their notes. He is due for a visit and labs; the front desk will reach out to schedule.

documents.title: Time for a check-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Sean, it has been six months since your last visit and you are due for your diabetes check and labs. Please call or reply with a few times that work. Morning appointments are open next month.
